posts.cooked:
Our group had a little bit of an ideological fight between the conservatives and the liberals.  Specifically, those who would like to consider card effects as conservatively as possible when ambiguous, and those who would like to stretch until a rule confines them.

 

The card that hit our group and caused a few fights was the Brain Burn card.  Its top text (using the current edition's wording):  "Put the Villain Trash on the bottom of the Villain Deck."

 

Our liberal players seized on this, and combined this with the following from the Rules and Clarifications file for SotM:  "When a player applies an effect that affects multiple cards, the player chooses what order the effects occur."  Their conclusion is that this means that Brain Burn allows them to target each card in the Villain Trash, and thus, choose the order of the Trash before it goes on bottom of the Deck.

 

The conservative players in the group believe that the Brain Burn card targets the Villain Trash specifically, and does not individually target each card in the Villain Trash.  This would then mean that the effect resolves instantly, with no race conditions--the Villain Trash is turned upside down in its current state, and placed immediately under the Villain Deck.

 

Which ruling is correct?

Given that a players deck, trash, and hand are define as individual entities in the game, I would say it targets the entire trash at one time.  Thus, the entire trash as a single unit is moved to the bottom of the deck.

I go with this idea because it is the simpler of the two, and the idea of the design of the game is to be as simple as possible in such situations. It also makes other cards much simpler as well, such as NightMist's card which allows a deck to be switched with it's trash, (The deck becoems the trash, and the trash becomes the deck, as an atomic swap. It would be a nightmare (and potentially an undesireble time extension of the game) to move each pile from one to the other one card at a time.)

But maybe that's just the conservatie in me talking, heheheh.

As many times as I've played Visionary, I have never used Brain Burn.

It's usually a dead card, but can prevent game loss against Terralunar Blade (esp. on Advanced), makes a great turn-1 play against the Chairman, counteracts Forced Deployment as very little else can, and can reduce the hassle of dealing with Omnitron, Citizen Dawn, and so forth, so it has lots of potential applications, though all of them pretty niche and only a few really worth the damage you take.  (If only you could Wrest yourself…)  Usually I'll discard it to Enlighten, but not always.  I do wish it was a singleton.

We used Brain Burn to stop the The Matriarch from flipping, since it refills the deck without shuffling the trash in.

Stealth Bot was valiant in her sacrifice.

 

This is how I view this card and how you would sort the deck.

1.  There is no rule stopping you from re-ordering the villain trash.

2.  Brain burn has you put the trash on the bottom of the deck.

3.  Even if Brain Burn did not allow reordering, you could reorder the villain trash directly before playing Brain Burn, then just put it under the deck.

 

So basically even if the card doesn't allow you to stack the deck, you can still do it, since you can stack the trash right before playing the card.

Unless we get a ruling that trash order cannot be alterred by players this will be an option, with the amount of cards that shuffle the trash before revealling I don't expect that ruling to ever be made.

It's also often useful against Omnitron, short-circuits several of Apostate's more annoying cards (though it's risky since he might Profane Summon into the redecked Relics, rather than getting a Relic Spirit killed and move them from the trash), and was extremely good in a recent La Capitan fight ("All Together Now!  Wait, why can't I remember where I parked my ship?").  Against Voss it can cancel Forced Deployment if the timing is just right, and The Matriarch is mentioned below.  The Dreamer and Ambuscade shuffle their trash into their deck a lot anyway, so it does basically nothing but help them; it's a terrible idea against Gloomweaver (unless his trash has no Relics and you just want to stop a Vast Following of Cultists and Zombies), and does pretty much nothing against the rest of the villains (besides kill Visionary, which might occasionally be desireable if you want her incap ability sooner and she's clearly got a short lifespan anyhow - I could especially see this happening if Brain Burn is the only card in her hand, and an incapped hero earlier in the turn order has no more useful options than letting Visi play a card, which kills her and thus gives her things to do on her turn besides Enlighten someone).
